analysis: The closest option integrates international relations theory, comparative and European politics, international and EU law, and global history. International macroeconomics, public economics and policy analysis connect interdependence, collective choice and institutions. Modern History, History of Empires and Ways of War provide distinctive temporal lenses. Empirical design, econometrics and qualitative research support investigation. Rhetorical communication and sociology contribute argumentation and social context.

The security option replaces international macroeconomics, microeconomic behaviour, public economics, rhetoric and introductory sociology with criminal justice, youth resilience to extremism, ethics, data science and historical research. The criminal law gateway precedes the corrected autumn offering. The concentration examines political violence, peacebuilding, international legal obligations and security across domestic and international settings. The history seminar adds original historical research without substituting for a disciplinary specialization or thesis.

Climate governance connects the programme’s cooperation question to international relations, public international law and EU institutions. Climate science, life-cycle assessment, renewable-system design and recovery of resources develop evidence for policy choices. Water courses connect nature-based measures to flood risk, legal frameworks and justice. Indigenous histories add environmental sovereignty and ecological knowledge, and climate communication examines public debate. The fixed early research course was replaced through a revised environmental selection, not through a changed offering.

The plans differ by 37.5, 97.5 and 105 EC in both directions. The broad programme prioritises breadth across IR, economics, history and methods. The security programme prioritises conflict, law, prevention and accountability. The climate programme prioritises sustainability evidence and institutions that respond to shared environmental problems. Introductory Dutch alone cannot support the independent language candidate. A separate introductory IR unit, global change survey, language continuation, IR Today and third-year specialization have no sufficiently close additional scheduled counterpart.

BENECON312.contribution: provides advanced quantitative modelling and inference for political-economy evidence
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

alignment.rationale: Students choose a 30 EC minor, with approval where required.
Students choose one of four faculty-wide courses. The topics depend on their choice.
Both compare political institutions, regime types and political participation.
Both use international relations theories to analyse state behaviour, cooperation and conflict.
Both study European Union institutions and decision-making. Groningen also integrates EU law in this course.
Groningen requires a separate introduction before its theory course. UCR’s theory course covers some introductory ground.
Groningen gives current international affairs a separate course.
Both study treaties, state responsibilities and the role of international organisations.
Both examine causes of armed conflict, security and responses to violence. UCR gives particular attention to peacebuilding.
Both introduce how markets work and how policy affects economic outcomes.
Both examine economic interdependence across borders. UCR focuses on macroeconomics, while Groningen studies the politics of the global economy.
Both cover historical changes that shape world politics, including war, decolonisation and globalisation.
Both use the history of power across borders to explain the present. UCR focuses on empires.
The specialization module focuses on an international relations theme and prepares students for the linked thesis.
Groningen requires a thesis linked to the specialization module. Independent research at UCR is optional.
Both introduce statistical reasoning for empirical questions. UCR also teaches research design.
Both teach research design and methods. UCR focuses on qualitative social research, while Groningen applies methods to international relations.
Groningen requires the first course in a modern-language sequence. UCR offers introductory Dutch.
Groningen normally continues the same language. The UCR options have no equivalent progression.
Groningen studies global change through several perspectives. UCR’s climate courses address environmental change and its consequences.
